title: API Stability Contract & Client Migration Timeline for Legacy Generate/Stream Endpoints
creator: Asha Patel
description: Executive summary: This PRD defines the contract and timeline for phasing out the legacy /v0/generate and multiplexed streaming endpoints and guiding clients to the unified inference API. The deliverable is a prescriptive migration timeline, stability guarantees for each phase (SLO windows and compatibility guarantees), clear acceptance criteria for SDKs and server behavior, and a customer-facing migration playbook. The output will enable predictable client upgrades while protecting production traffic via circuit breakers, telemetry gates, and rollback paths.
background: We maintain two parallel transport surfaces: legacy sync/multiplexed streaming endpoints used by long-standing customers and a newer unified inference API. Past efforts to nudge clients have been fragmented. This initiative consolidates a single, company-endorsed migration pathway that reduces runtime complexity, improves maintainability, and unlocks runtime optimizations (continuous batching, KV cache reuse). Previous migration artifacts (see links) informed compatibility shims; however, we will adopt a timeboxed sunsetting approach with explicit stability contracts so customers can plan upgrades confidently.
scope_changes: Initial scope: define migration contract, publish timelines, implement graceful-compat shim for 6 months, update SDKs and docs, instrument telemetry and gating. Out of scope: rewriting third-party partner SDKs, one-off custom migration for regulated customers (handled via enterprise onboarding). If a customer requires extended support, create a separate enterprise migration agreement outside this PRD.
requirements:
1) Public migration timeline with milestone dates and rollback criteria.
2) Compatibility shim that translates legacy multiplexed stream to unified chunked streaming with max 6-month support window.
3) SDK releases (JS/Python/Go) with helper functions and deprecation warnings before enforcement.
4) Telemetry dashboards capturing broken clients, fallback frequency, and per-customer latency regressions.
5) Circuit breaker policy that rejects legacy endpoints at enforcement date with clear error codes and migration hints.
6) Customer communications package (emails, in-console banners, migration guide, sample code).
7) Acceptance testing harness and canary rollout plan for enforcement.
8) Rollback playbook for post-enforcement incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Public migration timeline published and linked from console and docs with at least 90 days notice before enforcement start.
Compatibility shim deployed to hosted plane with telemetry; can be toggled per-region and per-customer.
Official SDKs (JS/Python/Go) include migration helpers, emit deprecation warnings, and have passing migration tests in CI.
Telemetry surfaces show migration progress: 95% of calls migrated for targeted PLG cohort before enforcement in that cohort's region.
Automated integration tests cover canonical streaming and sync flows and validate semantic equivalence for 95% of sampled requests.
Circuit breaker returns documented HTTP error codes and migration hints; compliance verified in canary traffic.
Customer-facing migration guide includes code samples, diagnostic checklist, and rollback instructions; internal support runbook published.
Post-enforcement SLA: less than 1% customer-impact incidents attributable to migration within 30 days of enforcement, or rollback will be triggered.
migration_timeline: Phase 0 — Discovery & Telemetry (Weeks 0-4): finalize instrumentation events, enumerate active clients, identify high-risk customers.
Phase 1 — Communication & SDK Prep (Weeks 4-8): publish migration plan, release SDKs with warnings, begin direct outreach to top 50 customers.
Phase 2 — Compatibility Shim Beta (Weeks 8-12): deploy shim in beta region, run stability tests, invite opt-in customers to shadow mode.
Phase 3 — Gradual Enforcement (Weeks 12-20): enable shim-by-default, begin rejecting new legacy connections in opt-in cohorts, monitor telemetry gates.
Phase 4 — Enforcement & Sunsetting (Weeks 20-32): enforce circuit breaker for all hosted customers; maintain shim for additional 3 months for enterprise accounts upon request.
Phase 5 — Remove Shim (Month 8-9): remove compatibility shim entirely after monitoring window and enterprise exceptions resolved.
rollout_playbook: Pre-enforcement checklist: 1) Confirm SDK builds and docs published. 2) Release console banners and email templates. 3) Execute top-50 customer outreach and schedule migration assist sessions. 4) Run canary traffic for 72 hours; verify error budgets and rollback hooks. Enforcement day steps: 1) Set circuit breaker to soft-enforce (return warning codes 299 with migration hints) for 1 hour. 2) If metrics stable, flip to hard-enforce (410/429 with migration instructions). 3) Escalation on increased error budget consumption: pause enforcement and initiate rollback via runbook. Post-enforcement: 1) Open special support lane, 2) daily migration progress report for 30 days, 3) prepare retrospective and lessons learned.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Key metrics: legacy endpoint call volume, percent migrated per-customer, error rates (4xx/5xx), p95 latency changes vs baseline, shim usage rate, rollback triggers count. Dashboards: per-region migration progress, top failing clients, SDK-version adoption over time. Telemetry gates: if p95 latency increases >25% or error rate >2% above baseline for more than 30 minutes in canary cohorts, pause enforcement and run rollback.
rollback_and_fallback: Rollback triggers: sustained error budget breach, customer-segment critical degradation, or data loss detected. Rollback actions: 1) Re-enable shim / revert circuit breaker to prior state within 15 minutes. 2) Notify stakeholders and impacted customers with timeline and remediation steps. 3) Create incident post-mortem within 72 hours. Fallback behavior: where possible, return structured error payloads that include diagnostic IDs, suggested code snippets to detect and retry against unified endpoints, and links to support resources.
docs_and_sdk_actions: Docs: single migration guide with three migration patterns (small-batch apps, streaming-heavy apps, embeddings+generate hybrid). Include code diffs and automated lint rules. SDKs: add MigrationHelper APIs, release minor semver with deprecation warnings, and include CLI tool to scan usage and produce a migration report per repo. CI checks: add gating job that fails if legacy endpoints detected in new commits for codebases in our SDK-monitored orgs.
